finding: A torn move marker makes plan() hand out a new /cd path on every call and never start a creation
why: The `except (OSError, ValueError)` branch returns `fresh(...)` without recording it or calling `spawn`, and the marker stays unreadable, so every later call for that session repeats the same dead end and the session can never be moved.
fix: On ValueError unlink the corrupt marker and re-plan (as the dead-owner branch does), or record the fresh move; then change test_h2_move.py:639 to expect a started creation.
evidence: h2_move.py:125-126 `except (OSError, ValueError): return fresh(root, name, pane, facts, marker)` (HEAD 6c84b5d1); the marker is written by `open(marker, "x")` then `json.dump` (lines ~114-119), so a kill between them leaves an empty file, as does a loser at line 120 reading the winner's marker mid-write; test_h2_move.py:639 `test_an_unreadable_marker_names_a_fresh_path_and_starts_nothing` asserts `not spawned`. Reached by reading; not run.

finding: The --skip-build-gate assertion passes when the creator run failed before provisioning
why: The check only asserts that the npm stub log is empty. A run that exits at argument parsing or any earlier error also leaves the log empty, and nothing asserts that OUT6 produced a worktree.
fix: Assert RC6 is 0 and that the worktree dir exists before the empty-log check, as the --no-npm case on the next lines does with `[[ -d "$WT7" ]]`.
evidence: create-worktree-smoke.sh:199-203 `OUT6="$(run_cwt ... --skip-build-gate npm 2>...)"` ... `[[ ! -s "$NPM_LOG" ]] && ok "--skip-build-gate reaches the provisioner" || bad ...`; contrast :210 `[[ -d "$WT7" ]] && ok "deprecated flags still produce a worktree"`.

finding: The test name claims a template without {name} never reuses one branch, but only one worktree is created
why: A fixed-branch regression (two names colliding on `team/fixed`) would only show on a second creation, which the test never makes.

finding: The orphan-worktree test branches on the installed git version and checks a different contract on each branch
why: Only one branch runs per machine, so each is verified on a subset of machines, and an early `return` hides the other.
fix: Split into two tests, one skipped below git 2.42 and one skipped at or above it.
evidence: test_create_worktree_name.py:470-474 `if version < (2, 42): assert done.returncode != 0 and "AFK_ALLOW_PROTECTED=1" in done.stderr; return` then `assert done.returncode == 0`.

finding: The live-lock test proves a negative with a fixed 6-second sleep
why: A creator slower than 6 seconds to reach the lock loop, or a lock-breaking regression that finishes after the poll, would pass; the on-disk check is the only stronger signal.
fix: Poll for a positive signal (the creator process blocked in the wait loop) or assert after the lock is released that the creation began only then.
evidence: test_create_worktree_name.py:507-509 `time.sleep(6)` / `assert waiting.poll() is None, "a live holder's lock must not be broken"` / `assert not (repo / ".claude" / "worktrees" / "waits").exists()`.

evidence: test_create_worktree_placement.py:191-194 `@pytest.mark.parametrize("case", range(4))` ... `rule, breaks = list(_refusal_cases(tmp_path, home, listed, root))[case]`.
